1160: They demanded to board first, then had me hold the plane while they admired their reflection in the window.
1161: They wanted the whole cabin to themselves and offered to buy every empty seat so no one could sit near them.
1162: They paid me a small fortune to forget their face, then reminded me three times how unforgettable it was.
1163: They insisted the seatbelt sign was beneath them and asked if I could turn it off just for their row.
1164: They knocked on the cockpit door to tell me I was flying too slowly for someone as important as them.
1165: They tipped me to announce their arrival over the speakers, then listened hard for applause that never came.
1166: They asked whether the plane could be repainted in a color that matched their coat before takeoff.
1167: They demanded first boarding, first meal, first everything, and grew impatient waiting to be first at nothing.
1168: They handed me a thick roll of cash and asked, very seriously, if I could keep the flight a secret from the sky.
1169: They complained the clouds outside were not arranged grandly enough for a traveler of their standing.
1170: They made me hold everyone at the gate while they arranged their coat, their scarf, and their opinion of the seat.
1171: They paid extra to be forgotten, then signed the payment with a flourish so I would remember the signature.
1172: They demanded the whole hold for their cases, then asked, sincerely, where everyone else should keep theirs.
1173: They stood at the front of the line and announced that lines were for people, not for someone like them.
1174: They asked me to circle once above the city so the whole world could see they had arrived.
1175: They boarded first, took a bow to the empty rows, and asked when the rest of their audience would arrive.
1176: They pressed money into my hand for silence, then loudly described exactly how rich they were.
1177: They wanted a private staircase, a private aisle, and a private cloud, and were annoyed I could only offer the aisle.
1178: They demanded to be the only name on the passenger list, and asked me to erase everyone else who ever flew.
1179: They paid me to forget their face and left behind a portrait of it, in case forgetting proved difficult.
1180: They took the best seat before anyone else could reach it, then asked if we had a better seat than the best one.
1181: They ordered one of everything on the cart, tasted each once, and declared the whole cart a disappointment.
1182: They complained the cabin was not grand enough and asked whether we kept a fancier cabin hidden somewhere.
1183: They demanded the window, the aisle, and the seat in between, all for one very self-important passenger.
1184: They rang the call button just to have me admire their outfit, then rang again in case I had missed it.
1185: They asked for the finest drink we carried, then a finer one, then were upset we did not carry the finest.
1186: They wanted their meal served on real silver and looked genuinely wounded when I brought a plastic fork.
1187: They took the whole blanket cart and built themselves a little throne, then asked for a footrest to match.
1188: They ordered every dessert we had, ate the top off each, and asked what we served to truly important people.
1189: They insisted the seat recline further than it could, and blamed me personally when the engineering refused.
1190: They asked me to announce that a very distinguished passenger was aboard, without mentioning it was them.
1191: They wanted the meal, the extra meal, the crew's meal, and then complained none of them tasted grand.
1192: They demanded the seat with the best view and grew sulky when every window showed the same sky.
1193: They asked for a pillow, received one, and stared at it as though I had personally chosen the wrong one.
1194: They took the seat reserved for someone else, sat like it had always been theirs, and asked for a menu.
1195: They ordered everything twice, once to eat and once to look at, and left the looking one untouched.
1196: They found the seat too ordinary and asked me to do something about it, though they could not say what.
1197: They wanted a whole row cleared so their coat could travel comfortably in the seat beside them.
1198: They asked the crew to introduce themselves one by one, then forgot each name the moment it was said.
1199: They demanded the front seat, then decided the front was not far enough forward, and sulked the whole way.
